explain.say: Imagine some older kids you really want to impress dare you to skip class. Your heart starts pounding. That push is called peer pressure, which means feeling pushed by people your age. Look at Rahul's worried face.

faq.q: What can I say when friends pressure me?
faq.a: Keep it short: No thanks. Not my thing. I have to go. You can also suggest something else, or make an excuse like: My mum would ground me forever.
asks: Tell me about the Say no
How do I say no to my friends?

faq.q: How do I know when something does not feel right?
faq.a: Your body often tells you first: a tight tummy, fast heart or a worried thought. If you would not want a parent to see it, that is a big clue.
asks: Tell me about the Tummy says no

faq.q: Who can I tell about peer pressure?
faq.a: A parent or carer, a teacher, a school counsellor, a grandparent, or another adult you trust. If someone threatens you, tell an adult straight away.
asks: Tell me about the Tell someone

faq.q: What if they call me boring for saying no?
faq.a: Real friends accept your choices. Saying no takes courage, and people often respect it more than you expect.
asks: Will they stop being my friend if I say no?

faq.a: No. Friends can also push you in good ways, like joining a sports team, studying together or being kind.

facts: A 2005 study by Margo Gardner and Laurence Steinberg found that teenagers took more risks in a driving game when friends were watching.
Peer pressure can be positive too, such as friends encouraging each other to study, exercise or volunteer.
